category: 2026 DRC-Uganda-France BDBV Outbreak (Active — PHEIC; deadliest and largest ever recorded in DRC)
killed: 2,516 confirmed DRC / 2 confirmed Uganda = 2,518 confirmed total
injured: 2,774 surviving confirmed cases; ~837-840 currently hospitalized in isolation, 1,152 recovered (DRC); Uganda outbreak closed 28 July with 18 recoveries
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO / UN News / Al Jazeera — 20–21 August 2026
note: DRC: 5,290 confirmed cases across ~54-55 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces as of 19 August, published 20 August (81 new cases: Ituri 56, North Kivu 18, Haut-Uélé 7); 2,516 confirmed deaths; crude national CFR ~47.6%, up from ~20% in early June, reaching approximately 70% in North Kivu province specifically. Uganda: 20 confirmed cases (2 deaths, 18 recoveries), outbreak formally declared over 28 July 2026. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO estimates true DRC case count could be up to 4x higher than reported. Most deaths continue to occur in communities away from treatment centers; UN said half of all deaths in the outbreak occurred in just the last 20 days. 160 confirmed cases among healthcare workers with 43 deaths (~27% CFR). Death toll passed 2,500 around 21 August. On 16 August the death toll surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak, making this the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide behind the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic. A second WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting was held 18 August; Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said 'we must be frank: the epidemic is far from being under control.' In Bunia, Ituri, a mob attacked a health response team on 18 August, torching ambulances amid rising community mistrust; over 260 attacks on health workers have been recorded across six months, eight killed. On 20 August WHO/Africa CDC announced release of 70,000 Ervebo vaccine doses to DRC (20,000 for a Phase 3 Bundibugyo cross-protection trial, 50,000 for frontline/health workers) — the human trial had not yet launched as of 21 August, with a mid-September target. UN Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis warned on 21 August that response funding 'will run out' within weeks; US pledged an additional $80M (21 August) for bed capacity and burials, on top of $242M pledged 5 August, bringing total US assistance above $512M.
